decisions.reason: SOL preserves the sideways feint and folds the waiting-for-this-moment image into the movement.

SOL keeps the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s surprise.

H006 preserves the point that anyone would be caught off guard.
The rhetorical question keeps the sense that no Disciple would abandon an injured Master.
SOL preserves that the mage attack is what startled him even more.
“There was no doubt” is retained immediately before the movement in H010.
The veering movement and renewed charge are retained in H010.
SOL preserves the route and target while combining the adjacent movement description.

The tangle of questions is retained in H013.
The source says he thrust out a hand; SOL changes the physical action to thrusting out his sword.

SOL keeps the strike’s speed, the slowing moment, and the threat to Jin Taekyung’s back.

SOL retains the earthquake impact, smoke, steam, and the fist’s blinding light-flames.
SOL clearly identifies the man steadily pushing back the sword despite its Force.
The question is an idiomatic rendering of the challenge to take one’s eyes off him.
The source says the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s gaze sank; “hardened” changes that reaction.
The “too late” beat is retained at the start of H026.
SOL preserves that surprise and carelessness let Jin Taekyung escape.
The coffin taunt and address as Senior are preserved.
“Told me something” preserves the setup without changing its meaning.
SOL preserves the fiercer flames, the earlier Internal Injury, and his scorching breath.
“Wild little brat” and “extraordinary” preserve the source’s mixed fondness and praise.
The old-man self-reference and threat to burn them all are preserved naturally.
SOL keeps the sword being pushed back and distinguishes that from merely exerting all his strength.
“History behind the name Fire King” preserves the title’s accumulated history.
The source says this spirit is shown only by those fighting to protect something precious; SOL drops that limiting emphasis.
The source explicitly says not to be reborn as a human again; SOL omits “again.”
SOL keeps the ghostly blue, hellish fire in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
SOL preserves the momentary sense of being overwhelmed and the clenched teeth.
The vanished respectful address and rougher tone are retained.
The broadened smile and the opponent’s loss of composure are both retained.

The insult and refusal to keep hearing “Senior” are preserved in direct, natural dialogue.
The reversal of the balance of power is retained in H043.

The breath and forehead-vein details are retained in H045.
SOL retains his breath, visible strain, feet digging into the ground, and refusal to retreat.
The source’s “No—” correction is a distinct beat; SOL drops it.
SOL preserves the incredulous request to hold out for half a quarter-hour.
SOL keeps the insolent disciple abandoning his revered Master like a worn-out rag.
The smile is separated into its own beat; BASE already includes it in H048.
The complaint about being treated as a feeble old man keeps its annoyed, affectionate voice.
The advantage is stated in H052, so the deletion does not lose the source’s assessment.
SOL preserves the spent internal energy and the Demon Lord’s limit-breaking power.
The hundred-and-twenty-year span is stated in H054.
SOL retains the full hundred and twenty years and their struggle.
“Even himself” preserves the source’s self-struggle; the loneliness beat is carried in the same passage.
“Not anymore” preserves the turn away from his former loneliness.
“Something worth protecting with his life” preserves the life-at-stake resolve.
The source explicitly says he will wait for the person he is addressing; SOL drops that object.
The source’s “That was why” explicitly links his resolve to what came before; SOL drops the causal link.
“He could not” completes the prior statement that he would not break.
SOL keeps the clash and wavering flames, folding in the following roar from H062.
The smile’s survival is preserved, with its owner clear from the surrounding passage.
“Again and again” naturally preserves the repeated clashing and mingling.
The awl image and the distant fight behind him are preserved.
The source emphasizes the continuing roar and force’s aftermath; SOL makes the source of the shock waves less precise.
“His face” naturally refers to the Old Master just named.
The half-quarter-hour duration is stated in H068.
SOL retains the short duration and the tea-time comparison.
The risk of death in a superhuman fight is preserved in direct, natural phrasing.
SOL keeps the necessity of moving forward rather than turning back to check on Jeok Cheongang.

The reason for changing direction and leaving Jeok Cheongang is stated in H073.
SOL preserves both the Magic’s continued effect and the possibility that he will keep growing stronger.
The possibility of further growth is retained in H073.
SOL preserves the causal link between cutting off the Magic and turning the tide.
“As I’d expected” is an explicit narrative cue that SOL drops.
The passing weapons and dangerously close flashes are preserved.
SOL keeps the weapon list and introduces the two shared traits without changing the sense.

The source describes light flowing over the blades; “shone” drops that image.
The contrast that it was not just a few is retained at the start of H083.
The number of enemies and their Sword Energy level are preserved.
SOL retains the especially powerful presence at the center of the group.
“Enclosed from head to toe” preserves the full-body black armor.
SOL preserves that his title is unknown and that his former self is lost.

“My heart sank” preserves the sudden heaviness and the formidable-obstacle context.

SOL preserves the rush of air, the contrast with his light feet, and his forward charge.

The spear’s flashing arc cutting across the back of the neck preserves the action.
SOL naturally conveys that the strike did not go deep enough to kill him.
The narrator’s lack of carelessness is stated in H096.
The urgency is retained by “Every second counted” in H096.
The source specifies the spear’s trajectory and timing; “aim” is not the same physical detail.
SOL preserves Magic’s many variables without changing their role in the failed calculation.
The small level gap’s greater significance among superhumans is preserved.
SOL preserves the increase in speed and strength compared with the previous strike.

SOL keeps the sharpened rush, lightning-like descent, and space-cutting blade.

“Spurt” conveys the blood spurting from the strikes.
The blood across his body is stated in H105.
SOL preserves the cuts and the failed attempt to dodge in time.
“They’d been too fast” preserves the realization that the attackers were faster.
The source compares their strength with a moment earlier; “Just now” does not preserve that comparison.
The clear observation is stated in H109.
SOL retains the sudden increase in the blades’ speed and force.
The narrator’s feeling of the encirclement and energy pulse is stated in H111.
SOL preserves the surrounding Black Ghost and Peak masters and the energy pulse from the hill.
The source is conjectural (“They must be trying”); SOL makes their intent certain.
The immediate danger context remains clear without repeating “at this moment.”
The circle of mages and their sense of danger are retained in one sentence.
The mages’ fear for their lives is retained in H114.
“Me. Them.” preserves the source’s self-and-others contrast.
The “me and them” contrast is retained in H116.
The source names Will and desperation; SOL narrows desperation to wanting to live.
The inwardly spoken command and forward effort are preserved.
The source says more than a hundred; “a hundred or so” does not preserve that quantity.
“Had to get past” preserves the necessity expressed by “absolutely had to.”
The source says all distances vanished; SOL narrows this to a single distance.
SOL drops the destructive flashes coloring the surroundings and omits that the bolt is lightning.
The narrator’s acknowledgment that he knew is retained in H125.
The one-against-many imbalance and the clear strength difference are preserved.
The source says what is visible to the eye is not everything; SOL narrows this to what the narrator personally sees.
“Get past” naturally preserves the contrast between advancing and blocking the way.
The contrast between protecting something and forgetting what to protect is preserved.
SOL retains the loss of Will, desperation, and duty; the emphasis on “duty” is compatible with the source.
The source contrasts “I am not [like them]”; “I hadn’t” ambiguously continues the previous sentence instead.
The reason he can risk his life is stated in H132.
SOL preserves knowing the difference and fighting at the cost of his life and with all his soul.
“Through the air” is a natural rendering of the spearhead tearing through space.
“Summon Fire Dragon Armor” is a natural command with the glossary-protected item name intact.
